extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A synthetic texture dataset created using text-to-image models and a refinement pipeline. It contains 246,285 texture images across 56 texture classes and is designed to be high-quality, diverse, and representative of real textures.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak and Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created in three steps: generating texture-specific prompts using combinations of artistically informed descriptors across texture classes, using those prompts in adapted Stable Diffusion text-to-image pipelines to generate images, and then refining/filtering the outputs through frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consisted of constructed text prompts made from texture classes and artistically informed descriptors, which were used as inputs to Stable Diffusion pipelines to generate texture images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluations were conducted on the dataset at each stage of the refinement process to assess image quality and representativeness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports analysis from human evaluations showing that each refinement stage improved quality and representativeness, with overall gains of 3.4% in quality and 4.5% in representativeness.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses model texture bias and notes that the dataset is used to analyze texture-object associations for measuring texture bias in object classification models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Prior texture research is limited by small, manually collected datasets and traditional synthesis methods that require seed images and lack textual descriptions, restricting diversity, scalability, and semantic control.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to support a broad range of texture-based tasks, large-scale texture analysis, evaluation of model generalization on texture data, and analysis of texture-object associations and texture bias.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Regenerated images that were flagged by the NSFW filter to maintain a consistent number of images; retained only the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff values, applied in a balanced manner across texture classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Excluded images flagged as NSFW from the final dataset and applied a three-stage refinement/filtering process: frequency analysis/filtering to remove object-like images, patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images, and CLIP score filtering to ensure alignment with prompts.
